newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers firm as Iraq tensions flare.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers firm as Iraq tensions flare.

text.p: North American bunker prices firmed on supportive fundamentals and as U.N.-Iraq tensions deepened in the Middle East, traders said Thursday.
Fear of sharply higher prices saw shipowners attempting to cover forward requirements, while sellers quoted higher to guard against expensive replacement costs.
"Buyers are buying as far out as possible, some 10-12 days ahead which is unusual," a West Coast trader said, noting it was a function of confusion over where bids/offers were.
Prices have stayed high in all bunker centers and have not cooled since Iraq attacked Kurds in northern Iraq last week.
New York Harbor 380 CST rose to $120/122 a tonne, up $8 from two days ago. The 180 CST grade was quoted at $124/129.
The Norfolk hub stood around similar levels compared with New York, with 380 CST at $122/123, and 180 CST at $125/128.
On the Gulf Coast, sentiment was less panicky with more cargoes expected to filter in from Venezuela soon, although inventories remain tight, traders said.
Houston 380 CST was at $113/115 a tonne, and 180 CST was at $115/118 a tonne. Los Angeles 380 CST was at $113/115 a tonne, and 180 CST was pegged at $117/119 a tonne.
-- Jacqueline Wong, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1620
